senses.head: To cover the inside of a coat, a bag, or a box with another material
examples: They line the winter coats with flannel.
She lined the jacket with cheap silk.
The boots are lined with wool.

senses.head: To stand or be arranged in a row along something
examples: Oak trees line both sides of the street.
Fans lined the sidewalk for six blocks.
The hallway is lined with family photos.

entries.русский: подбивать подкладкой, ставить на подкладку; стоять вдоль, выстраиваться вдоль; тянуться вдоль
entries.contrast: You line something with a material, and the inner layer itself is the lining.

entries.meaning: Cuff has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He likes to cuff his jeans above his boots.
She cuffed the sleeves of his big sweater twice.
The pants came back cuffed and pressed.
The officer cuffed him and read him his rights.
They cuff everyone before the transport.
He was cuffed and put in the back of the car.

senses.head: To turn the bottom of a sleeve or a pant leg up into a fold
examples: He likes to cuff his jeans above his boots.
She cuffed the sleeves of his big sweater twice.
The pants came back cuffed and pressed.

senses.head: To put handcuffs on someone
examples: The officer cuffed him and read him his rights.
They cuff everyone before the transport.
He was cuffed and put in the back of the car.

entries.русский: подворачивать (штанину, рукав), закатать; надевать наручники, заковать в наручники

entries.meaning: To get small folds and creases in cloth, or to put them there. ---
examples: Linen wrinkles if you look at it.
The shirt wrinkled badly in the suitcase.
He showed up in a wrinkled jacket.
entries.contrast: The w is silent: RING-kuhl.

entries.meaning: To press a sharp line into cloth, or to get an unwanted fold in it. ---
examples: Marines crease their trousers razor sharp.
He creased the slacks down the front.
Her dress was badly creased after the flight.

entries.meaning: Unfold has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Unfold the shirt carefully so it does not wrinkle.
She unfolded the dress and hung it by the window.
The napkin had been unfolded and left on the chair.
The scandal unfolded over several months.
We watched the story unfold on live television.
Events were still unfolding when we went to press.

senses.head: To open out something that has been folded
examples: Unfold the shirt carefully so it does not wrinkle.
She unfolded the dress and hung it by the window.
The napkin had been unfolded and left on the chair.

senses.head: To develop or happen gradually over a period of time
examples: The scandal unfolded over several months.
We watched the story unfold on live television.
Events were still unfolding when we went to press.

entries.русский: разворачивать, расправлять, развернуть; разворачиваться, развиваться (о событиях)

entries.meaning: To put two things together, or to wear one item with another. ---
examples: Pair the gray blazer with dark jeans.
She paired the socks as she folded them.
That skirt is usually paired with boots.
entries.русский: подбирать в пару, сочетать, сочетать с
entries.contrast: You pair one thing with another. Pair, pear the fruit, and pare meaning to peel all sound alike.

entries.meaning: Separate has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Separate the whites from the darks.
She separated the wool items before washing.
The delicates are separated into a mesh bag.
Couples who separate often still share the kids' schedule.
They separated last spring after eleven years.
He has been separated from his wife since March.
Attention to detail separates a good cook from a great one.
One point separated the two teams at the buzzer.
The finalists were separated by less than a second.

senses.head: To divide things into groups, or to keep them apart
examples: Separate the whites from the darks.
She separated the wool items before washing.
The delicates are separated into a mesh bag.

senses.head: To stop living together as a couple without being divorced yet
examples: Couples who separate often still share the kids' schedule.
They separated last spring after eleven years.
He has been separated from his wife since March.

senses.head: To be the quality that makes one person or thing different from another
examples: Attention to detail separates a good cook from a great one.
One point separated the two teams at the buzzer.
The finalists were separated by less than a second.

entries.русский: разделять, отделять, разделить; расходиться, разойтись; разъезжаться (о супругах); отличать, выделять (среди других)
entries.contrast: The verb ends in /eɪt/, SEP-uh-rayt; the adjective separate is SEP-rit. There is an a in the middle: sep-a-rate.

entries.meaning: Match has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Those shoes do not match the belt.
She matched the scarf to her coat.
They showed up in matching sweaters.
No other store can match that price.
He matched the world record on his second try.
The company has matched every dollar she put into her 401(k).

senses.head: To look right together, or to find something that goes with something else
examples: Those shoes do not match the belt.
She matched the scarf to her coat.
They showed up in matching sweaters.

senses.head: To be equal to something, or to do as well as it
examples: No other store can match that price.
He matched the world record on his second try.
The company has matched every dollar she put into her 401(k).

entries.русский: подходить, сочетаться; подбирать в тон; не уступать, сравняться; соответствовать (по уровню)
entries.contrast: The third person adds -es: matches. You match one thing to or with another.

entries.meaning: Clash has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Orange and pink clash, but she wears them anyway.
The tie clashed with his shirt.
Those two patterns are clashing badly.
The two senators clash over spending every year.
Protesters clashed with police downtown.
The coach and the owner have clashed repeatedly this season.

senses.head: To look bad together, especially two colors or patterns
examples: Orange and pink clash, but she wears them anyway.
The tie clashed with his shirt.
Those two patterns are clashing badly.

senses.head: To fight or argue openly with someone
examples: The two senators clash over spending every year.
Protesters clashed with police downtown.
The coach and the owner have clashed repeatedly this season.

entries.русский: не сочетаться, дисгармонировать; сталкиваться, вступать в конфликт; спорить
entries.contrast: One color clashes with another.

entries.meaning: To go well with something and make it look better. ---
examples: A gray tie would complement that suit.
The blue scarf complemented her eyes.
The pieces were chosen to be complemented by simple jewelry.
entries.contrast: Complement, with an e, means goes well with. Compliment, with an i, means kind words. They sound the same.

entries.meaning: To be clearly different from something beside it, or to set two things side by side to show the difference. ---
examples: White stitching contrasts nicely with black leather.
The designer contrasted heavy wool with thin silk.
A contrasting collar makes a plain shirt look custom.
entries.contrast: The verb is stressed on the second syllable, kuhn-TRAST; the noun is KAHN-trast. One thing contrasts with another.

entries.meaning: To look good on a particular person, or to be right for them. ---
examples: That color really suits you.
The short haircut suited her.
He is not suited to a job with a dress code.
entries.contrast: Suit means it looks good on you; fit means it is the right size. A jacket can fit and still not suit you.

entries.meaning: To arrange clothes or hair to create a particular look. ---
examples: She can style one dress five different ways.
They styled the shoot in 1970s clothes.
His hair was styled for the photograph.

entries.meaning: Pose has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Pose by the window where the light is better.
They posed in their graduation gowns.
She was posing for the camera in her new coat.
The chemicals pose a serious risk to workers.
She posed a question no one could answer.
The new rules have posed a real problem for small farms.

senses.head: To hold a position so that someone can photograph or paint you
examples: Pose by the window where the light is better.
They posed in their graduation gowns.
She was posing for the camera in her new coat.

senses.head: To create a problem, a risk, or a question that someone has to deal with
examples: The chemicals pose a serious risk to workers.
She posed a question no one could answer.
The new rules have posed a real problem for small farms.

entries.русский: позировать, принимать позу; представлять (угрозу), создавать (проблему); ставить, задавать (вопрос)

entries.meaning: To show something off openly so that everyone notices it. ---
examples: He likes to flaunt his expensive watches.
She flaunted the new boots all week.
They were flaunting their designer bags on the boardwalk.
entries.contrast: Flaunt, to show off, is not flout, to break a rule openly.

entries.meaning: To make one feature more noticeable than the rest. ---
examples: A belt will accentuate your waist.
The dark trim accentuated his shoulders.
Her height was accentuated by the long coat.

entries.meaning: To hang down loosely because the shape is gone. ---
examples: Cheap knits sag at the knees.
The pockets sagged from all the keys he carried.
His jeans were sagging below his hips.
entries.contrast: The g doubles: sag → sagged, sagging.

entries.meaning: To rub the skin until it is sore. ---
examples: A wet collar will chafe.
The backpack strap chafed her shoulder.
His heels were chafed raw by the new boots.

entries.meaning: To pull at something with a short, sharp movement. ---
examples: Do not tug at the loose thread.
She tugged her skirt down as she stood up.
He kept tugging at his collar all through dinner.
entries.contrast: The g doubles: tug → tugged, tugging. You tug at something.

entries.meaning: To move loosely back and forth in the air. ---
examples: Loose shirts flap in this wind.
His open coat flapped as he ran for the bus.
The laundry was flapping on the line.
entries.contrast: The p doubles: flap → flapped, flapping.

entries.meaning: Embellish has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They embellish the jackets with beads by hand.
She embellished a plain dress with ribbon.
The collar is embellished with tiny crystals.
He always embellishes the story a little.
She embellished her résumé and got caught.
The tale has been embellished with every retelling.

senses.head: To add decoration to something plain
examples: They embellish the jackets with beads by hand.
She embellished a plain dress with ribbon.
The collar is embellished with tiny crystals.

senses.head: To make a story more interesting by adding details that are not true
examples: He always embellishes the story a little.
She embellished her résumé and got caught.
The tale has been embellished with every retelling.

entries.meaning: To treat something so that water cannot get through it.
examples: Waterproof your boots before the first snow.
He waterproofed the jacket with a spray.
The seams have been waterproofed at the factory.
